memory_candidates.text: For labelled/Kripke-world tableau termination where a world-creating rule (F(A->B)) copies parent formulas via persistence, the literature-standard measure is a LEXICOGRAPHIC / Dershowitz-Manna multiset order with the number of created worlds (bounded by 2^|subformulas|) as the dominant component -- NOT a flat count of unexpanded compounds. Canonical source: Garg, Genovese & Negri, 'Countermodels from Sequent Calculi in Multi-Modal Logics', LICS 2012 (Sfor-set-containment). The worlds-free G4ip formula-weight measure (Dyckhoff 1992; Troelstra-Schwichtenberg Basic Proof Theory 2nd ed 4.3; Negri-von Plato Structural Proof Theory 5.5) does NOT transfer because it has no worlds.

The 2^(2n) finite-model / mosaic bound (Caleiro-Vigano-Volpe 2013; filtration in Chagrov-Zakharyaschev) bounds the DEDUPLICATED model size (distinct worlds x forced-sets), NOT the raw step count of an un-deduplicated tableau. A labelled procedure without a loop-check / Sfor-containment dedup can take 2^Theta(n^2) steps because compounds copied by persistence re-expand at every world and the beta-branchings multiply. The literature's dedup is precisely what makes step-count = model-size; without it, fuel of order 2^(2n) is insufficient. This is why intuitionistic tableau decision procedures deduplicate.
